full_judgment: 5. The respondent No. I in its affidavit-in-opposition stated„ that the "no objection certificate" as granted by the Ministry of Information is not a licence to run Television Broadcasting Channel through Satellite and Terrestrial net work and that the writ petitioners have no legal character and locus-standi to seek allocation of frequency and grant of licence and in the absence of formal licence from the Ministry of information the writ petitioners cannot approach the respondent No. 1 for allocation of frequency and grant of licence therefor and this writ petition is misconceived and premature one and that the frequency spectrum is very limited national resource, which is very cautiously used and that the petitioners cannot claim allocation of frequency as of right and that the respondent No. 1 has to scrutinize and examine the availability of this national resource and also prevent interfacing of use of frequency by the different users and this involves national interest and accordingly before issuance of any licence for broadcasting service the Ministry of Information should obtain from the respondent No. I a' report as to the availability of the frequency for allocation and that in view of the conflicting claim, conflicting interfaces and objection raised by the BTV, the issue of allocation has been taken up by the Ministry of Information for resolving the dispute; and the matter is still pending before the Ministry of Information and that the petitioners ought to have obtained formal licence for TV broadcasting from the Respondent No. 2 before applying to BTRC for allocation for frequency and that the fate of allocation of frequency depends on the petitioners holding of valid licence and availability of frequency spectrum subject to fulfillment of all legal requirements under the said Act and till such licence is granted question of giving permission for import of machinery does not arise and that the importation of machinery is governed by the provisions of Import Control Act, 1950 and the 13-ritc is not concerned with granting of licence for import of machinery and that the Respondent No. I issues licence for 1'V broadcasting and also grants allocation of frequency and the allocation of frequency falls under different chapter requiring
